---
title: "Exercise · Design the Metaphor"
---

A short, guided task. Complete it before moving on to the next lesson.

## Starting point

Use the `concept.md` you wrote for the ticketing system in the
[Lesson 2 exercise](../02-find-the-technical-truth/exercise.qmd), or use the
following brief concept if you did not complete it:

> The support desk has: Customers who submit tickets, a Ticket Queue that holds
> them, a Dispatcher that assigns tickets to Agents by category, Agents who work
> tickets, and a Notification System that alerts customers on resolution.

## Task

1. **Choose a world.** Pick a metaphorical world for the ticketing system.
   Consider: detective agency, post office, hospital triage, call centre, or
   another world that fits the request → dispatch → work → resolve flow.

2. **Write the mapping table.** Create a table with columns: Technical Model,
   Metaphor, Why it fits. Map every entity from the concept to its counterpart.

3. **Game the map.** Walk through each key fact from your concept and verify the
   metaphor respects it. Write down any conflicts you find and how you resolve
   them.

## Format for the mapping table

| Technical model | Metaphor | Why it fits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer | ... | ... |
| Ticket Queue | ... | ... |
| Dispatcher | ... | ... |
| Agent | ... | ... |
| Category | ... | ... |
| Status transitions | ... | ... |
| Notification | ... | ... |

## Success criteria

- [ ] You chose a world and can justify why it fits the system's flow.
- [ ] Your mapping table covers every entity in the concept.
- [ ] You gamed the map and documented any conflicts and their resolutions.
- [ ] No key fact from the concept is contradicted by the metaphor.

## Reflect

- Did any entity resist being mapped? What does that tell you about the world
  you chose?
- Would a different world make the mapping more natural?
- Did you find yourself changing the metaphor to fit the model, or the model to
  fit the metaphor?
